title: skills.victorsaly.com/sideshot: choose the page's structure
question: The look is settled (your monochrome frame, SideShot's ink and marigold). Pick how the page is built. Every option leads with the real before/after pictures and ends at the install command.

options.label: The page is the mark
options.lineage: SideShot's own mark: two squares, before in ink, after in marigold
options.thesis: The whole page splits like the logo: a before half and an after half, scrolling in step.
options.viewport: Left half: 'Before: you read a diff.' Right half, marigold rule: 'After: you see it.' The real #151 pictures under each; the install command sits across the seam.
options.risk: On a phone the halves stack, so the side-by-side lives only on wide screens.

options.label: Drag to see the change
options.thesis: One real picture fills the first screen; you drag the divider and the change appears under your hand.
options.viewport: Wordmark and one line on top, the #151 gate full width with a draggable marigold divider, install command right under it.
options.risk: A slider is a familiar device; it lands only because the picture is real and the rings show.

regions.label: SideShot · See the change. Side by side.

options.label: The page is a pull request
options.lineage: a GitHub PR description and its diff
options.thesis: The page reads like the PR SideShot writes into: a title, the table, and the install as the last added line.
options.viewport: A PR header 'SideShot this PR', then the real before/after table as GitHub shows it, then '+ npx skills add victorsaly/sideshot -g'.
options.risk: Developers get the joke fast; it must not outlast its clarity for someone who has never opened a PR table.
